children: Friday's U.S. employment report will show whether the labor market remains in its "low hire, low fire" equilibrium, with slow hiring offset by limited layoffs and a declining labor force, keeping unemployment broadly stable, First Citizens Bank's Phil Neuhart says in a note. "The key data to watch include nonfarm payrolls, the unemployment rate, the size of the labor force, and revisions to prior months," the head of market and economic research says. A meaningful decline in payrolls or a shrinking labor force would be early signs that labor market stagnation is giving way to broader weakness, he says. Analysts in a Wall Street Journal poll forecast the addition of 53,000 jobs in August. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
